clue.text: Guide to old French fashion

explanation.surface: A handbook to bygone Parisian styles of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a reference book that guides you to names and addresses; Directoire was the style of dress and furniture under the French Directory of the 1790s.

clue.text: There's the bell for gym

parts.note: the missing word goes before 'bell' to make a weight used in gym exercise

explanation.walkthrough: The bell meant is the gym weight, not a school bell calling pupils to class.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumb-bell is a short bar with weights used in physical training; dumb means silent, as an unrung bell is.

clue.text: Lady Macbeth caught in Ulster ?

parts.note: Lady Macbeth is seen with bloody hands, a culprit caught in the act, and the emblem of Ulster is a red hand

explanation.walkthrough: The Red Hand of Ulster is the badge of the northern Irish province.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in the act of a crime, as Lady Macbeth's bloodied hands betray her; the Red Hand is Ulster's heraldic symbol.

clue.text: Pet of greenstuff addicts

parts.note: cos is a variety of lettuce
a set is a group of devotees, as in the jet set

explanation.surface: A lettuce fanatic's favourite animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is a noun here: a cosset is a lamb reared by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosset is a hand-reared lamb, a household favourite animal.

clue.text: Instrument of propaganda

parts.note: a newspaper speaking for a party is its mouthpiece, and the word also names a keyboard instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A party newspaper is called its official mouthpiece; the same word is the pipe-driven musical instrument.

clue.text: The key to knowledge ?

parts.note: a famous American university shares its name with a well-known brand of lock and key

explanation.definitionFit: Yale is both an Ivy League university, a seat of learning, and a make of cylinder lock and key.

clue.text: Dad goes West for fruit

parts.note: papa is a childish word for a father
W is the standard abbreviation for West on a compass

explanation.surface: Father heads off westward in search of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawpaw or papaw is a tropical fruit, also called papaya.

clue.text: Would this clubman choose so northerly a venue ?

parts.note: to pick is to choose
Wick is a town on the far north-east coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: Would a member of a club opt to meet so far north?
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Pickwick founded the Pickwick Club in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pickwick is the founder of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's first novel.

clue.text: Fold in apple a tiny bit

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: Wrap a tiny piece of apple into a fold of pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold sewn or pressed into cloth.

clue.text: A little bedside support for the old ticker

definitions.text: A little bedside support for the old ticker

parts.words: A little bedside support for the old ticker
parts.note: the ticker is a pocket timepiece, not the heart, and the support is a small stand to hang it on by the bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'the old ticker' is slang for the heart, suggesting medicine, but here it is a pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stand to hold a pocket timepiece overnight by the bed.

clue.text: Old musical styles for poems in plenty

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for a great many
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Ancient ways of making music produced plenty of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ODES inside M, the Roman thousand standing for 'plenty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The church modes (Dorian, Lydian and the rest) were the scale patterns of early music.

clue.text: Midas's badge a bird ?

parts.note: King Midas turned everything he touched to gold, so gold is his emblem
a crest is a heraldic badge

explanation.surface: Would the golden-touch king's coat of arms feature a bird?
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is a tiny European songbird with a yellow stripe on its head.

clue.text: Measureless in Xanadu

parts.note: Coleridge's Kubla Khan has the river Alph run through hollows underground 'measureless to man' in Xanadu

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a fill-in-the-blank from Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan, set in Xanadu.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's line is 'Through caverns measureless to man', so the clue quotes the adjective that the poem applies to these underground hollows.

clue.text: Change of hair-style

explanation.surface: A new way of doing one's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to make a change; a switch is also a hairpiece of false hair added to a style.

clue.text: Hungry birds get a golden emmet amid bulbs

indicators.note: the golden and emmet pieces sit in the middle of the word for bulbs

parts.note: corms are bulb-like stems, as of a crocus
or is the heraldic word for gold
emmet is an old word for an ant

explanation.surface: Ravenous birds seize a gilded ant among the flower bulbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic word for gold, and emmet a dialect name for an ant; the birds' greed gives the English idiom of a cormorant as a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: Cormorants are greedy fish-eating seabirds, so their name means a glutton.

clue.text: "There was a danced", said Beatrice

parts.note: in Much Ado About Nothing Beatrice says she was born when a heavenly body danced in the sky; the gap takes its name

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank from Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice's line is 'there was a star danced, and under that was I born', so the gap is a heavenly body.

clue.text: Divine in outsize makes difference

indicators.note: the letters for the divine are placed inside those for outsize

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a theologian or divine

explanation.surface: A clergyman in extra-large clothing stands out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Divine is a noun here, a churchman, given as DD; the scan prints 'makes a difference', the 'a' lost in transcription.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds, as in 'it makes no odds', means the difference or inequality between things.

clue.text: Bucentaur ?

parts.note: the Bucentaur was the ceremonial barge of the Doges of Venice, a vessel used on occasions of state

explanation.walkthrough: The Bucentaur carried the Doge out each year to wed Venice to the sea, so it is literally a state craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, the answer is a vessel of state; as one, it means the art of government.

clue.text: Harry upsets foreign state

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets means the word is turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: etat is the French word for state; that the letters also sit inside the English word state is a coincidence, as 'foreign' asks for the French word

explanation.surface: A man named Harry overturns a foreign government.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Tate was a British music-hall comedian; 'upsets' turns ETAT, French for state.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Tate was a famous British music-hall comedian, so Harry is his first name.

clue.text: Tell shot the first above the second, with what point ?

definitions.text: Tell shot the first above the second, with what point ?

parts.words: Tell shot the first above the second, with what point ?
parts.note: William Tell shot a bolt over his son's skull to split the apple; the first word over the second names the tip of the bolt

explanation.walkthrough: In the legend William Tell shot an apple from his son's head with a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tip of an arrow; the two halves are what Tell shot and what it flew above.

clue.text: The indictment does not accuse William of perjury

definitions.text: The indictment does not accuse William of perjury

parts.words: The indictment does not accuse William of perjury
parts.note: a grand jury's endorsement of a charge is its name, and read as two words it calls a man nicknamed Bill honest

explanation.walkthrough: Bill is short for William; true means honest, so no perjury.
explanation.definitionFit: A true bill was a grand jury's finding that an indictment was well founded; split, it says William is honest.

clue.text: Leading divines exerting a restraining influence

explanation.surface: Senior clergy keep their flock in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moderator presides over the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland or a presbytery; moderators are also people or things that restrain and temper.

clue.text: Does this dish make the horse flourish ?

definitions.text: Does this dish make the horse flourish ?

parts.words: Does this dish make the horse flourish ?
parts.note: this word put before 'dish' makes a word for flourish, and it is also a mash fed to horses

explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' looks like 'thrive' but is the verb meaning to wave a sword about, which the answer plus 'dish' spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of grain fed to horses as a mash, and joined to the clue's 'dish' it gives a word meaning wave or flourish.

clue.text: Counsel formal notice

explanation.surface: A lawyer's official letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance or counsel, and in commerce an advice is a formal notification of a transaction.

clue.text: Outstanding assistance

explanation.surface: Exceptional help.
explanation.definitionFit: Carving in relief stands out from its background; relief is also aid given to those in need.

clue.text: Even after fifty she has a distinctive air

indicators.note: after says the word for the air comes behind the fifty

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an aura is a distinctive atmosphere around a person

explanation.surface: A woman still has a special charm past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'she' is the definition: Laura is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a girl's name, so she can be any woman called that.

clue.text: Trouble in the stable area or, the fields ?

indicators.note: the word for trouble goes inside the word for the stable area

parts.note: mews were stables round a yard, in London now converted to houses
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Is the commotion in the stable yard, or out in the fields?
explanation.walkthrough: A mews is a British row of former stables round a yard; the comma after 'or' is surface punctuation and 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadows are grassy fields, often kept for hay.

clue.text: Was a native so encouraged to return to his heath ?

definitions.text: Was a native so encouraged to return to his heath ?

parts.words: Was a native so encouraged to return to his heath ?
parts.note: Hardy's novel The Return of the Native is set on a Wessex heath whose name sounds like 'egged on'

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy's hero Clym Yeobright returns to the heath of his birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Egdon Heath is the setting of Hardy's The Return of the Native, and its name sounds like egged on, meaning encouraged.

clue.text: Style of the Roman century here

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
hic is the Latin word for here

explanation.surface: Elegance came to Rome a hundred years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are Latin: C for centum, a hundred, and hic, here.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish elegance.

clue.text: Pixie upset copper and ran away

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for the pixie upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: an elf is a small mischievous fairy
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: An overturned fairy scuttled off with a policeman's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ELF to FLE; D stood for the old penny, a copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fled is the past tense of flee, to run from danger.

clue.text: He is round when well fed

indicators.note: well signals the letters of the preceding words are worked over into good order

explanation.surface: Someone turns plump once properly fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' is the anagram signal on HE IS ROUND; the surface also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nourished is to have been given food, the same as fed.

clue.text: Perfect, says one who lays cards on the table

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to deal is to give out cards onto the table

explanation.surface: A card dealer announces his hand is flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The dealer says 'I deal', which runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Stop here for stabling

explanation.surface: A halt for the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to come to a halt, and a stall is a compartment where a horse is kept.

clue.text: Strove to get the faithful little girl cared for

parts.note: Con is a pet form of Constance, a girl's name meaning constant or faithful
tended means looked after

explanation.surface: Struggled so that a loyal daughter would be looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: The faithful girl is Constance, whose name means steadfast; her short form Con gives the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to struggle or compete, so strove is its past tense.
